title: Operator Decision Frequency and Escalation Scheduler — Playbook & Simulation Kit
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview
=======

This playbook defines the Operator Decision Frequency & Escalation Scheduler (ODF-ES), a platform-level component and set of operational practices designed to: reduce operator alert noise, protect operator attention budgets, and ensure escalations happen at controlled cadence while preserving customer SLOs. It includes an operator-friendly scheduler, safe defaults, a small simulation kit for validation, and a dashboard spec for monitoring the system impact.

Why we built it
----------------
- Operators were receiving bursts of repetitive escalations for the same degradation events causing cognitive overload and delayed responses.
- We need a mechanism to: de-duplicate, schedule, and rate-limit escalation delivery while retaining deterministic routing for critical faults.
- ODF-ES balances two opposing constraints: minimize time-to-human for critical incidents and minimize operator burnout caused by high-frequency noise.

Goals & SLO alignment
----------------------
- Primary goal: keep mean time to actionable human (MTAH) under 8 minutes for P1s, 30 minutes for P2s while limiting operator interruption frequency to <= 6 distinct interrupting alerts per 24h per operator on-call.
- Secondary goal: reduce duplicate escalations by 80% for the same incident fingerprint within a 10-minute window.
- Tertiary: provide deterministic, auditable scheduling policy and simulation harness for playbook rollouts.

Key concepts
-------------
- Incident fingerprint: a normalized key (service, region, fingerprint-hash) used to identify related alerts.
- Escalation budget: per-operator soft cap measured as "interrupts per rolling 24h". Budget refill policy is configurable per rotation.
- Decision frequency: the minimum interval between successive human-facing escalations for the same fingerprint. Default: 10 minutes for P1, 30 minutes for P2.
- Circuit-breaker: a fast-path that bypasses scheduling for high-confidence, high-severity signals.

Architecture (high level)
------------------------
1. Alert producers (prometheus-alerts, ingestion webhooks) -> normalized event bus (kafka).
2. Event enrichers: attach fingerprint, model confidence, tenant impact, and SLO score.
3. ODF-ES Scheduler: de-duplicates, computes decision frequency, consults operator budgets and routing rules.
4. Notification layer: routed to Slack/PagerDuty/email with per-channel rate limits and grouping.
5. Dashboard and simulation harness for validation and post-rollout metrics.

Diagram (text)
---------------
Alert sources -> Kafka -> Enricher -> Scheduler -> Notifier -> Paging system
               
Configuration table (parameters)
------------------------------
| parameter | default | description | impact if tightened |
|-----------|---------|-------------|---------------------|
| decision_frequency.p1 | 600s | min seconds between escalations for same fingerprint, P1 | faster response, more interrupts |
| decision_frequency.p2 | 1800s | as above for P2 | fewer interrupts, slower reaction |
| operator_budget_per_24h | 6 | soft interrupts cap per operator per 24h | protects operators; may delay noncritical escalations |
| circuit_breaker_threshold | 0.95 | probability/confidence above which scheduler bypasses delay | ensures urgent faults surface immediately |
| group_window | 120s | window to batch alerts with same fingerprint | reduces messages, may increase message size |
| max_queued_per_fingerprint | 10 | backpressure cap | prevents unbounded queue growth |

(Use the YAML snippet below to configure the scheduler for a service)

Example scheduler config (YAML)
-------------------------------
apiVersion: v1
kind: ODFSchedulerConfig
metadata:
  service: "runtime-prefix-cache"
spec:
  decision_frequency:
    P1: 600 # seconds
    P2: 1800
  operator_budget_per_24h: 6
  circuit_breaker_threshold: 0.96
  group_window_seconds: 120
  routing_policies:
    - name: "regional-default"
      route: "team-runtime-ops"
      fallback: "team-platform-sre"

Runbook: Deploying the scheduler (safe rollout)
------------------------------------------------
1. Create a feature-flagged ODF-ES deployment in staging.
2. Apply a conservative config (P1=600, P2=1800, budget=8) and enable simulation mode.
3. Run the attached simulation kit for 48h against a replay of the last-30-day alert stream. See "Simulation recipe" section.
4. Validate: duplicate rate reduction >= 60%, MTAH for P1 < 12 minutes.
5. Gradually flip the feature flag in canary (10% of regional traffic), monitor dashboards for 2 business days.
6. Roll forward to 50%, validate, then to 100% if no regressions.
7. Conduct a post-rollout review in next SRE retro.

Operator flow: what an SRE sees
-------------------------------
- If fingerprint arrives and operator budget is available: immediate escalation (grouped if within group_window).
- If budget exhausted: escalation is queued and a single digest is sent to the next rotation after the budget refill event, with a link to the running incident.
- If circuit-breaker conditions met: immediate escalation regardless of budget.

PromQL examples for SLO & scheduler metrics
------------------------------------------
- P1 mean full MTAH (reporting):
  sum by (service) (rate(odf_es_mta_histogram_sum{severity="P1"}[1h])) / sum by (service) (rate(odf_es_mta_histogram_count{severity="P1"}[1h]))

- Duplicate escalation rate (10m window):
  rate(odf_es_duplicate_count[10m]) / rate(odf_es_total_escalations[10m])

- Operator interrupt count per oncall (24h):
  increase(odf_es_operator_interrupts_total[24h])

Alertmanager routing snippet (example)
-------------------------------------
receivers:
  - name: "team-runtime-ops"
    slack_configs:
      - channel: "#runtime-ops-critical"
        send_resolved: true
route:
  group_by: [fingerprint, service]
  group_wait: 30s
  group_interval: 2m
  repeat_interval: 4h

Simulation recipe (quick start)
-------------------------------
1. Obtain the last-30-day alert export from the alert bus: CLI: 
   $ odfctl export --window 30d --out=alerts-30d.ndjson
2. Run the harness: 
   $ odf-sim --config examples/staging-config.yaml --input alerts-30d.ndjson --out sim-results/
3. Run the analysis script to compute metrics: 
   $ python tools/sim-analysis.py --dir sim-results --metrics duplicate_rate,mta,paging_delay
4. Inspect dashboards (see "Dashboards" below) and the generated CSV to confirm target reductions.

Dashboard spec: panels to create
-------------------------------
- Escalations per fingerprint (heatmap)
- Duplicate escalation rate (timeseries)
- Operator interrupts per oncall (bar)
- Queue depth per fingerprint (timeseries + alert if > 50 for 1h)
- MTAH distribution by severity (histogram)
- Simulation vs production comparison pane

Acceptance tests & validation checks
------------------------------------
1. Unit tests for fingerprint function (coverage >= 95%).
2. Integration tests: simulated traffic shows duplicate_rate reduced >= 50% compared to baseline.
3. Load test: scheduler handles 10k alerts/min sustained with median enqueue latency < 2s.
4. Canary safety checks (automated): no P1 MTAH regression > 50% over baseline in 4h window.

Operator playbook (during an active degradation)
-----------------------------------------------
1. When a P1 page arrives, follow the P1 incident checklist in the standard incident runbook.
2. If multiple operators receive grouped messages, the first responder should claim the running incident in the incident manager UI.
3. To force immediate re-alerting for an in-flight fingerprint (operator override): run CLI: 
   $ odfctl override --fingerprint <id> --action escalate-now --reason "operator-override"
4. If operator budget prevents escalation for a critical-seeming signal, use the incident manager "Escalate -> immediate" button; this triggers an audit log entry and bypasses the decision frequency.

Rollout timeline & responsibilities
-----------------------------------
- Owner: Platform Reliability team (team-platform-sre).
- Primary on-call reviewers during rollout: runtime-ops@redwood.com.
- Q1 2026: staging deployment and simulation validation.
- Q2 2026: canary (10% -> 50%) and runbook practice run.
- Q3 2026: global rollout and postmortem retro.

Retrospective template (to run 2 weeks after rollout)
-----------------------------------------------------
1. Summary: what we changed, config values, traffic % rolled.
2. Metrics: duplicate_rate, MTAH, operator interrupts, queue depth.
3. Incidents influenced by ODF-ES: list and classification.
4. Operator feedback: qualitative notes on cognitive load.
5. Action items and owners (deadline).
